messages.subject: geom_line() errors with new data
parts:
#here is some data
a=as.data.frame(cbind(x=1:10,y=c(1:5,5:1)))
b=5.5
c=2.5

#here's how to plot it using plot() and lines()
# (yes, this looks silly, but it's a simplification of
# other data I have)
plot(a$x,a$y)
lines(
x=c(min(a$x),b,max(a$x))
,y=c(min(a$y),c,min(a$y))
)

#here's an attempt to use qplot() & geom_line() to do the same
p=qplot(data=a,x=x,y=y)
p=p+geom_line(
aes(
x=c(min(a$x),b,max(a$x))
,y=c(min(a$y),c,min(a$y))
)
)
print(p)
# Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :
# arguments imply differing number of rows: 3, 10

#try with ggplot()
p=ggplot(data=a,aes(x=x,y=y))
p=p+geom_point()
p=p+geom_line(
aes(
x=c(min(a$x),b,max(a$x))
,y=c(min(a$y),c,min(a$y))
)
)
print(p)
# Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :
# arguments imply differing number of rows: 3, 10

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: geom_line() errors with new data
parts:
Hi,

> p=qplot(data=a,x=x,y=y)
> p=p+geom_line(
+ data=data.frame(
+ x=c(min(a$x),b,max(a$x))
+ ,y=c(min(a$y),c,min(a$y))
+ )
+ )
> p

works for me.

My guess is that you were misusing the aes() function, the description
of which reads,

"Aesthetic mappings describe how variables in the data are mapped to
visual properties (aesthetics) of geoms."

In other words, you passed some data instead of a description of how
the data should relate to the plot.

Hope this helps,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: geom_line() errors with new data
parts:
Thanks! On a related note, it seems that there's a strange naming error...

#use names "x" and "y"
a=as.data.frame(cbind(x=1:10,y=c(1:5,5:1)))
p=qplot(data=a,x=x,y=y)
print(p) #works ok
p=p+geom_line(
data=data.frame(
x=c(1,5.5,10)
,y=c(1,2.5,1)
)
)
print(p) #works ok

#use names "iv" & "dv"
a=as.data.frame(cbind(iv=1:10,dv=c(1:5,5:1)))
p=qplot(data=a,x=iv,y=dv)
print(p) #works ok
p=p+geom_line(
data=data.frame(
x=c(1,5.5,10)
,y=c(1,2.5,10)
)
)
print(p) #yields an error

#try ggplot()
p=ggplot(data=a,aes(x=iv,y=dv))+geom_point()
print(p) #works ok
p=p+geom_line(
data=data.frame(
x=c(1,5.5,10)
,y=c(1,2.5,10)
)
)
print(p) #yields an error

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: geom_line() errors with new data
parts:
I think you're still missing the aim of the aes() function. In your
second example you create a mapping between x and iv and y and dv. Any
subsequent layer will use this correspondence by default. So the
geom_line() layer tries to find some values called iv and dv in the
data and there are none of course. You can however specify a new
mapping explicitly for this layer,

>

That's a good explanation.

Preferably the mapping shouldn't depend on anything outside of the
plot/layer data. If you save this plot and reload it in another
session, it won't work because it won't have access to a, b, or c. If
I could figure out how to make this an error, I would.
